So "indonesia" here is not one reporting territory: the upstream layer-B country harmonization collapsed at least six distinct IIA reporting units — "dutch east indies", "dutch java and madura", "dutch east indies: outer provinces", "dutch sumatra", "dutch bali and lombok", "dutch java, madura and outer provinces" — into the single string "indonesia", with the survivor varying by item and even by year. That cannot be confirmed (it would attribute Java's output to the whole archipelago), cannot be fixed by a single reroute (some rows really are whole-DEI), and cannot be expressed as a split_reroute because the split is by series, not by year. The candidate wiki page (draft, 3,772 bytes, 5 citations) is accurate about the DEI's territory and I found nothing wrong in it; the defect is upstream of the polity DB, in label harmonization, so this belongs in quarantine for a human to resolve by re-deriving the assertion from the raw IIA country strings.
review.wiki_note: IIA data routed to this polity is NOT whole-Dutch-East-Indies: the upstream layer-B harmonization collapsed six distinct IIA reporting units into the label "indonesia". Sugar (median 1.42 Mt), soybeans and groundnuts are "dutch java and madura" only (~132,000 km2, 7% of this row's 1,877,243 km2); rubber area is an estate-only partial sum (1939: 615,700 ha routed vs the source's own DEI total of 1,329,500 ha, -54%; 1941-42 values are Java-Madura alone, ~5x low), while cotton, cacao, sesame, tea and tobacco do come from genuine "dutch east indies" series. Any use of this source's series under IDN-1800-1945 must be checked per item against the raw country string.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "india" agricultural-statistics label (1893-1913) to IND-1893-1914, a national British-India polity whose CShapes-derived polygon (~4.8M km²) covers the whole subcontinent under British paramountcy, including princely/native states. The wiki page (wiki_status: draft, so treated as hypothesis not evidence) makes a careful, well-cited argument that the *external political boundary* was constant across 1893-1914 (Durand Line 1893 and McMahon Line 1914 were frontier delimitations of territory already under British control, not sovereignty transfers) - this is corroborated independently by standard historical accounts of both events, which I accept. However, independent web research on the source side (official "Agricultural Statistics of India" series, which Mitchell's international historical statistics compiles from) turns up a genuine scope caveat the wiki page does not address: the official annual agricultural-statistics series was compiled primarily for directly-administered British Indian provinces, with princely-state acreage largely absent or only partially/inconsistently included, whereas the candidate's polygon area (~4.8M km²) represents the whole British-paramountcy territory including princely states (which held roughly 40% of the subcontinent's area). This is a potential sub-territory fold-up: the source's reporting territory may be narrower (British India proper) than the candidate polity's full territory. There is, however, no separate WHEP polity for "princely India" to reroute to, so IND-1893-1914 remains the only available and reasonable match - this is a best_available confirm, not a verified_equal one, both because of this coverage caveat and because a ~20-year span crossing two frontier-delimitation events (1893, 1913) is not automatically "constant" without independent corroboration beyond the draft page's own say-so. Staple magnitudes (rice 29.9M ha, wheat 9.9M ha) are plausible in scale for greater British India inclusive of Burma, not clearly pointing to either scope reading on their own.
verdict.wiki_note: Official "Agricultural Statistics of India," the primary source underlying Mitchell's India series in this period, was compiled mainly for directly-administered British Indian provinces; princely/native-state acreage was largely absent or only partially and inconsistently reported (per Blyn-type reconstructions vs. later broader compilations like Kurosaki's). The candidate's CShapes-derived polygon (~4.8M km²) covers the whole British-paramountcy territory including princely states (~40% of the subcontinent's area). This is a potential source-narrower-than-candidate scope gap the page does not discuss; no separate "princely India" polity exists to reroute to, so this remains the best available match, but the acreage/production totals may understate true full-territory magnitudes and should not be treated as complete British-India-plus-princely-states figures.

verdict.basis: The candidate's wiki page documents CShapes 2.0 recording Senegal as a constant-area colonial territory (~195,995.8 km²) from 1886-01-01 through the Mali Federation transition, with boundaries unchanged even through the 1959 Federation entry/exit and independence in 1960 — i.e. the reporting territory (French colonial Senegal) was geographically constant across the entire assertion's observed span (1886-1959). This is a component colony under French rule, not the wider AOF federation: the source's magnitudes (groundnuts ~487,500 t, cattle ~393,000 head, rice paddy 50,000 ha, maize 18,000 ha) are plausible for Senegal alone — Senegal was AOF's principal groundnut producer, and these figures are far too small to represent the whole multi-colony AOF federation (which would show cattle/livestock in the millions and groundnuts spread across several territories). No annexation, cession, or boundary change occurred within the observed span per CShapes, so the territory is both correct in scope (Senegal proper, not AOF or a sub-unit) and constant throughout.

The assertion routes FAO 1952 "Italy" (1937-1951) to candidate ITA-1919-2025, our single continuous Italy row (1919-2025, no internal split). The span 1937-1951 straddles a real territorial change: the Feb 1947 Treaty of Paris, under which Italy ceded Istria/parts of Dalmatia to Yugoslavia and ~268 sq mi to France. FAO's country-level series for Italy in a given year almost certainly reflects that year's actual borders (pre-1947 larger Italy including Istria for 1937-1946 rows, post-1947 smaller Italy for 1947-1951 rows), consistent with normal yearbook practice of reporting current-year national territory. Since WHEP's own database does not split Italy at 1947 (the wiki page itself raises this exact issue as an unresolved open question, oq-post-wwii-losses, and explicitly declines to split), there is no alternative existing polity to reroute or split-reroute to — ITA-1919-2025 is the only and best available match for the whole 1937-1951 span. Staple magnitudes (grapes ~2.87M ha, meat ~278k t, milk ~2.45M t) are all plausible in scale for interwar/postwar Italy (pop. ~42-47M), giving no sign of a scope mismatch (e.g., no evidence data includes colonies or excludes/includes Istria inconsistently with the label). Because the reporting territory did NOT stay constant across the observed span (1947 cession), this cannot be verified_equal even though no better candidate exists — it is best_available. The wiki page (draft status, but substantive: 5623 bytes, 12 source citations, no TODO markers) already documents this exact territorial-change issue in detail, so there is no new information to add via wiki_note.

review.basis: Numbers first. The FAO 1952 "Italy" levels are metropolitan-Italy scale, and they exclude both the colonial empire and any sub-national fold-up. Grapes ~2,868 kha of vine area only makes sense for the whole peninsula under Italy's characteristic promiscuous/mixed vine culture (contemporary Italian vine area, specialised plus mixed, ran ~3.0-3.6 Mha against ~12 Mha arable in a 310,000 km2 country); no single region or island could carry that, and no colony could add to it (Libya/Eritrea/Somalia grew negligible vine). Horses+mules+asses ~770k head, meat ~278 kt and milk ~2,450 kt are likewise per-capita and per-km2 plausible for a ~43M-person peninsular economy, an order of magnitude too large for a province and with no empire-sized surplus. The decisive independent check is the bundle's own verified source convention: FAO 1952 "population total" for Italy 1937 = 42,372k, which matches the 1936 census of the Kingdom of Italy proper (42.4M) and excludes the ~2.5M of Libya/AOI and the Dodecanese — so the label is metropolitan Italy, not the Italian Empire, and not a combined reporting unit. Fold-up in the other direction is ruled out by the same magnitudes. Hence the routing to ITA-1919-2025 is right, and no other existing polity fits (the Dodecanese is separately carried as ITAEG-1912-1947, consistent with FAO reporting it apart). It is best_available rather than verified_equal for one reason only: the reporting territory did not stay constant across 1937-1951. The 1937 figures are on pre-war borders including Venezia Giulia/Istria, Zara and Fiume (~8-9,000 km2, ~3% of area, plus disproportionate viticulture), while the 1951 figures are on post-Treaty-of-Paris (1947) borders after the cessions to Yugoslavia and France and the loss of Trieste's disputed zone. Our database does not split at 1947 (the candidate's own page raises this as open question oq-post-wwii-losses), so a single polity cannot equal the reporting territory over the whole span; the discrepancy is small but real and the honest label is best_available. The candidate page (draft, 5.6 kB, 12 citations) documents this territorial history and I used it only for corroboration of the 1947 losses, not for the scope verdict, which rests on the magnitudes and the population cross-check.
review.wiki_note: FAO 1952 reports "Italy" as metropolitan Italy only: its 1937 total population of 42,372k matches the 1936 census of the Kingdom proper and excludes Libya/AOI and the Dodecanese (carried separately here as ITAEG-1912-1947). This bears on oq-post-wwii-losses: within this row the 1937 series is on pre-war borders (incl. Venezia Giulia, Zara, Fiume) while the 1951 series is post-Treaty of Paris, so cross-period series on this row are not on a constant territory even though the step (~3% of area, more in vine area) is too small to show as a magnitude break.

verdict.basis: The IIA 'philippines' label for 1909-1945 reports on the Philippine archipelago as a single reporting territory (American colony through 1935, then Commonwealth, occupied by Japan 1942-1945, all on the same land area). The candidate PHL-1800-2025 covers the whole span as one row with CShapes feature 840 (1898 vintage) carried through unchanged; the wiki explicitly argues the 1898 and 1946 sovereignty transitions did not change the archipelago's extent. Staple magnitudes (abaca/manila fibre ~324k ha, tobacco ~69k ha, raw centrifugal sugar ~441k tonnes) are all plausible, well-attested Philippine export-crop scales under the same land base, with no sign of a step change indicating a territorial scope shift, and no sub-territory or entrepot signature (Philippines is itself the producing territory for these staples, not a transit point). No existing polity subdivides the Philippines for this period, so PHL-1800-2025 is the only candidate and it fits. However the observed span includes the Japanese occupation (1942-1945), which the routing instructions explicitly flag as an event that breaks constancy even when land extent is unchanged, so this is best_available rather than verified_equal despite territory itself never changing.

The assertion's observed span is 1949-1960, entirely inside the window between Indian independence/princely-state integration (completed 1947-1949) and the next two territorial changes documented on the candidate's own wiki page: Goa's annexation from Portugal (Dec 1961) and Sikkim's accession (1975). Both post-date the observed span, so they are irrelevant to this specific assertion even though the wiki page (thorough, well-cited, despite being labeled 'draft') treats them at length as caveats for the row's LATER years. Within 1949-1960 India's sovereign territory was stable and there is no combined-reporting, union-scope, or sub-territory fold-up concern (Mitchell's 'India' label at this date plainly means the Republic of India, not a colonial-era British India aggregate — partition was already complete in 1947). Staple magnitudes (millet ~15.8M ha, sorghum ~15.5M ha, barley ~3.1M ha) are large-country-scale figures consistent with subcontinental India and continuous with the neighbor segment IND-1947-1949 immediately preceding this row, supporting no scope discontinuity at the 1949 boundary. Given the reporting territory equals the candidate's territory and was constant across the whole observed 1949-1960 span, this is verified_equal rather than best_available.

The candidate NGA-1914-1960 is colonial Nigeria formed by amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates on 1914-01-01, running unchanged (per CShapes area, constant at 71.1 sq deg) until the 1961 Northern Cameroons incorporation — which falls after the observed data span ends (1959). Mitchell's "Nigeria" label for 1914-1959 is the standard national aggregate for this exact same territory. Staple magnitudes (cacao ~84,000 t, groundnuts ~297,000 t, cotton lint ~34,000 t, cattle ~2.9M head) are all plausible national totals for Nigeria's known colonial-era export profile, with no signs of entrepot inflation or sub-territory fold-up. Neighbor segments (NNI/SNI predecessor pre-1914, NGA-1960-1961 successor at 1960) confirm clean chain boundaries. The wiki page is reviewed status with 4 source citations (Biger-1995) and its territorial narrative is internally consistent and externally plausible.

review.basis: Numbers first: for a territory of ~923,000 km2 with roughly 20-35M people, the staples read as whole-colony aggregates, not a province and not an empire. Cocoa median 84,000 t matches Nigeria's known trajectory (~50k t in the 1930s rising past 100k t in the 1950s, the world's 2nd-3rd producer) and is far too large for any single Nigerian province or for the small Southern Cameroons plantations; groundnuts 297,000 t is the Kano/Northern trade at its documented scale; cotton lint 34,000 t and wild/plantation rubber 2,250 t are of the right order for the whole colony; cattle 2.9M head fits the northern herd (Nigeria ~6M by 1960), and would be geologically/agronomically absurd for the southern colony alone. So the implied scope is "all of Nigeria" — the candidate's scope — with no sub-territory fold-up and no entrepot signature (all five staples are things Nigeria genuinely produced). Continuity supports the same reporting basis: the label runs unbroken 1889-1959 across our 1914 split into NGA-1886-1914, i.e. Mitchell already treats pre-amalgamation Northern+Southern+Lagos as one "Nigeria" series, so the 1914 amalgamation is a purely administrative event with no reporting-territory step, and 46 distinct years with n=45-46 on cocoa/cotton/rubber indicates a single continuous compilation. The reviewed wiki page (2.8KB, 4 citations to biger-1995, no TODOs) independently agrees on the territory and dates, and I did not need it to reach the verdict. Why best_available rather than verified_equal: the reporting territory did not stay constant across 1914-1959. British Cameroons (~87,500 km2, our own separate polity BCM-1916-1961) came under British administration in 1916 and under mandate from 1922, sat inside the Nigerian customs area, and its returns were routinely folded into Nigerian Blue Book/trade statistics, while the candidate's CShapes-475 1914 polygon excludes it. That is roughly a 9% area expansion mid-span, so no single polity equals the reporting territory; NGA-1914-1960 is nonetheless the best available routing and the distortion to these staples is small (Cameroons' cocoa/banana output was a minor fraction). I could not read Mitchell's own territorial footnotes, hence medium rather than high confidence.
review.wiki_note: Mitchell's "Nigeria" series for 1922-1959 very likely includes British Cameroons (Northern and Southern Cameroons, ~87,500 km2), which was administered with Nigeria and inside its customs area, and whose returns were folded into Nigerian colonial statistics; the CShapes-475 1914 polygon used here excludes it, so the reporting territory is ~9% larger than the polygon from 1922 on. Flag a double-count risk against any independent series routed to BCM-1916-1961.

verdict.basis: Uruguay is a small, long-stable South American republic whose borders have not changed since independence in 1828 (Treaty of Montevideo, buffer state between Argentina and Brazil) -- no annexations, cessions, unions, or occupations occurred in 1860-1960 that would alter its reporting territory. The wiki page (draft status, but citing Biger 1995 and COW state-system data, 3 citations) documents stable borders throughout the polity's 198-year span, consistent with COW ccode=165 continuity. Mitchell's 'Uruguay' label for 1860-1960 has no plausible sub-national or union-scope ambiguity (unlike Sweden-Norway, Austria-Hungary, etc.) since Uruguay was never part of a larger reporting union and has no internal component large enough to be separately reported by Mitchell's world tables. Staple magnitudes (wine ~17,000t, beer ~7,760t, meat ~289,000t, milk ~556,000t, flax ~183,500ha) are all plausible in scale for a small agricultural/pastoral nation of Uruguay's size (~176,000 km2, per Biger 1995) and show no discontinuous jumps suggesting a territorial scope change across the observed decades. No known failure family (union scope, boundary vintage, combined reporting, sub-territory fold-up, entrepot re-export) applies: Uruguay is not a component of a larger polity, was not combined with another state under this label, and its livestock/dairy/grain products are indigenous to its own pampas, not re-exports through a transit port.

The IIA label "China, Taiwan Province of" is a modern administrative label (post-1949 ISO convention) retroactively applied by IIA/FAO to Taiwan-island agricultural statistics for the observed years 1909-1944. The candidate TWN-1895-1945 (Formosa, Japanese Taiwan) covers exactly this island territory (~36,193 km²), stable from the 1895 Treaty of Shimonoseki cession through the 1945 retrocession, with no boundary change in that interval — a single colonial administration (Taiwan Governor-General's Office) that reported its own agricultural/trade statistics separately from the Japanese home islands. The draft wiki page is well-documented (6 source citations, Biger 1995 area figure of 35,987 km² closely matching CShapes' 36,193 km², explicit sub-territory note distinguishing TWN from the much larger JPN-1895-1945 empire aggregate) and its territorial claim is independently corroborated by staple magnitudes: sugar raw centrifugal median 500,724 tonnes and tea 40,832 ha are consistent with well-documented Japanese-era Taiwan being a major colonial sugar and tea producer at that scale, not plausible for a fractional sub-region or for the whole Japanese Empire. No evidence of a mid-span territorial change (island extent fixed 1895-1945), so the whole observed span (1909-1944) maps to one constant, correctly-scoped candidate polity.

The candidate MAR-1911-1958's own wiki page contains a "Scope correction" (2026-07-24) establishing, from a prior assertion review of a different source (Mitchell), that this row's attached polygon is French Morocco specifically (350,268 km²) and NOT the whole Sherifian Empire/Morocco proper (~446,000 km², which also includes Spanish Morocco tracked separately as SMO-1912-1956 plus Tangier and Ifni). The IIA assertion here (rows=338, years 1911-1945, agricultural items: flax, tobacco, grapes, cotton seed, linseed) matches that same known pattern for international statistical-yearbook sources of this era: French and Spanish protectorate administrations each ran their own statistical services and reported separately to international bodies like the IIA, so a bare "Morocco" label most plausibly denotes the French zone, consistent with the candidate's actual (French-zone) territory. Staple magnitudes (grapes 24,000 ha, flax 17,000 ha, cotton seed 385 ha, linseed 11,000 tonnes) are modest and plausible for the French zone's arable agricultural belt (Gharb, Chaouia, Doukkala), not inflated in a way suggesting the whole protectorate+Spanish zone was folded in. Web search could not directly confirm IIA's own French/Spanish Morocco reporting split (no digitized-yearbook-level detail surfaced), so this rests on analogy to the already-established convention for a comparable source (Mitchell) rather than direct external verification of IIA itself. One year (1911) predates the Treaty of Fez (1912) establishing the protectorates, meaning for that single year "Morocco" would have denoted the still-unified sovereign sultanate rather than the French zone alone — a minor territorial-scope wrinkle within the 35-year span that, combined with the reliance on an analogous-source convention rather than direct IIA-specific confirmation, keeps this at best_available rather than verified_equal.

review.basis: Numbers first: I pulled the 340 IIA rows for label "morocco" from the raw consolidated source (/home/usuario/Nextcloud/WHEP_ERC 2025/Sources/datasets/processed_datasets/consolidated_datasets/mitchell/mitchell_juan_iia.csv) and from the layer-B parquet. The slice is minor crops only (flax 5k->52k ha 1915-1945, linseed 3-24k t, grapes 5.6k->26k ha, olives 50-105k t, wine area 0.8k->23k ha, oats 35-53k ha, cotton a few hundred ha). Working blind from levels: a territory with ~7M people and a few hundred thousand km2 of which the plains (Gharb, Chaouia, Doukkala, Haouz) carry all commercial cropping — i.e. exactly French Morocco (candidate polygon measured 350,268 km2, cshapes feature 600 @1912). The settler-driven series (vineyards 0.8k ha in 1922 growing tenfold by 1937; wartime flax expansion to ~50k ha in 1940-45) are French-zone phenomena; the Rif/Spanish zone had negligible commercial viticulture or fibre flax. Scope check both directions: the label is not a sub-territory of the candidate (no province/district reading), and the upward risk (French+Spanish combined) is immaterial to the levels — fao1952 in the same DB reports French vs Spanish Morocco separately for 1939-51 and the Spanish zone runs ~5-12% of the French one (sheep 595k vs 9,149k; cattle 254k vs 1,762k; population 1937 6.8M French zone), and no "spanish morocco"/"tanger" label exists anywhere in the IIA source, so the Spanish zone was simply not an IIA reporting unit. No entrepot/re-export issue (all field crops), no boundary-vintage step, and no continuity break at any of our period splits (the label's own span 1909-1945 sits entirely inside the candidate's 1911-1958, and there is no rival Morocco row for these years; SMO-1912-1956 carries the Spanish zone's own 55 rows, so no double count). Why best_available rather than verified_equal: (a) I could not find external documentation of the IIA yearbook's Morocco footnote, so French-zone-only vs French-zone-in-practice remains an inference from magnitudes and from the source's own footnote table (state/iia_territorial_notes.csv carries "french morocco" tenure notes 1928-1945, indicating the yearbook's Moroccan unit is the French protectorate); (b) the reporting territory was not constant across 1911-1945 — French statistical coverage tracked pacification, expanding from the coastal plains in the 1910s to the full protectorate only after 1934, which is visible as the 1915-1921 series being an order of magnitude below the 1930s levels for flax and grapes. The routing is right; the equality is approximate.
review.wiki_note: Data-quality break in the IIA slice, not in the territory: tobacco is internally consistent 1930-33 (92-222 ha, 141-314 t, ~1.5 t/ha) but from 1934 the area column collapses to 0 or exactly 1,000 ha while production jumps to 17,600-103,400 "tonnes" (up to 100 t/ha, agronomically impossible) — a unit/scale misparse from 1934 onward (likely quintals and '000 ha), which also affects flax 1945 (41,000 ha, 4,100 t). Also worth recording: the IIA rows for this polity are minor crops only (fibres, oilseeds, fruit, tobacco); Morocco's cereals and livestock in the same consolidated file come from Mitchell, so the two sources are complementary rather than overlapping here.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "zimbabwe" 1901-1952 series (cattle, maize, cotton, groundnuts, tobacco, goats, sheep) to ZWE-1900-1953 (Southern Rhodesia). The candidate's wiki page (draft, but backed by 4 citations to biger-1995, an external gazetteer) documents that Northern Rhodesia was separated from the Southern Rhodesia administrative unit by 1900 (CShapes cowcode=552 vs 551), and that CShapes records no territorial change for cowcode=552 across the entire 1900-1953 span (single polygon, area≈390,610 km2 per the polities_database.csv SRH-1953-1964 sibling row which shares the same cowcode/area). The 1923 shift to self-governing colony status was constitutional only, not territorial, per the page's own sourced claim. The neighbor_segments field shows the immediate post-span years (1953-1960) already route to SRH-1953-1964, the Federation-era Southern Rhodesia row with the identical cowcode 552 and area, confirming continuity of the same reporting territory across the WHEP row boundary rather than a change. Magnitudes (cattle ~2.3M head, maize ~110k t, tobacco ~3,550 t) are plausible for the settler-agriculture economy of colonial Southern Rhodesia alone (not requiring Northern Rhodesia's copper-belt territory to explain scale) and show no discontinuity pattern suggesting a scope change mid-span. Mitchell's African historical statistics conventionally report "Rhodesia/Zimbabwe" as Southern Rhodesia distinct from Northern Rhodesia for this period, consistent with the routing. No sub-territory fold-up or entrepot risk applies (this is the primary agricultural/pastoral producer territory itself, not a transit hub). Given both the polygon-family cross-check (same cowcode 552, same area 390,610 km2 recurring in SRH-1953-1964) and the external biger-1995 citations independently corroborate a constant Southern Rhodesia territory 1900-1953, this is a solid confirm with verified_equal.

Assertion routes FAO1952 "United States" 1931-1951 data to USA-1867-1959, whose territory (continental US + Alaska, ~9.4M km2) was stable across the entire 1867-1959 span with no territorial change occurring within the observed 1931-1951 window (Hawaii/Alaska statehood in 1959 is a status change, not territorial, and postdates the span; Philippines/Puerto Rico/Guam are tracked as separate WHEP rows and are not part of this reporting label). The bundle's source_conventions entry (independently verified 2026-08-14 against consolidated_layer_b.parquet) cross-checked FAO1952's "population total" indicator for the US at 128,961k in 1937 against the accepted continental US population (~128.8M), confirming the reporting territory is the mainland+Alaska US, not a broader or narrower unit. No magnitude discontinuity or scope ambiguity found for this label in this era (unlike Yemen/USSR-type combined-reporting cases). The wiki page is draft status with only 1 (self-referential, CSV-derived) source citation, so it is not itself treated as evidence, but its territorial narrative is independently corroborated by well-documented US history and the bundle's own population magnitude check.

The assertion routes Juan-panel crop rows labeled "Romania" for 1940-1946 to ROU-1940-1947, the reduced-territory Romania (~194,000 km2) after the three simultaneous 1940 cessions (Bessarabia+N.Bukovina to USSR, N.Transylvania to Hungary, S.Dobruja to Bulgaria) and before the 1947 Treaty of Paris restored N.Transylvania. The wiki page is "reviewed" with 7 sourced claims citing biger-1995 for each boundary-change date, and is candid about polygon-construction history (not just asserted, but reasoned through CShapes limitations and a stated GADM-county proxy with area cross-checks) -- this is a substantive, non-circular page. Magnitude continuity across the neighbor segments corroborates the routing independently: barley area drops from a median 1,590,150 ha (1920-1939, Greater Romania candidate ROU-1920-1940, 296,000 km2) to 554,250 ha (1940-1946, this candidate, 194,000 km2) and rye drops from 319,400 ha to 91,850 ha -- both consistent with losing Bessarabia/Bukovina, a major grain region, in 1940. The observed span (1940-1946) lies entirely inside the candidate's constant-territory period (1940-1947, ending only with the 1947 restoration), so the reporting territory did not change within the observed years -- this supports verified_equal rather than merely best_available. No sub-territory fold-up, entrepot, or combined-reporting concern applies; "Romania" here is a national-level agricultural series on the country's own post-1940 borders.

review.basis: I worked from the source's own per-year series (pulled the juan/Romania rows out of state/matched_rows.parquet) before reading any prose. The 1939->1940 step is decisive and rules out boundary-vintage carry-over: wheat 4,079k -> 2,078k ha (-49%), barley 1,096k -> 588k (-46%), maize 4,932k -> 3,567k (-28%), rye 448k -> 92k, potatoes 306k -> 142k. A loss of only Bessarabia + N. Bukovina + S. Dobruja (~52k of 295k km2, 18%) cannot produce a 46-49% fall in wheat/barley; the magnitudes require that Northern Transylvania (43k km2) is also out. So for 1940-43 the reporting territory is the ~194,000 km2 rump, i.e. exactly the candidate. Cross-check on the label's counterparties: Hungary in the same source shows NO 1940-44 enlargement (wheat 1,407-1,544k ha, indistinguishable from Trianon 1936-39 at 1,483-1,642k), so N. Transylvania's output is not folded into Hungary either - consistent with the rump-Romania reading rather than double counting. Scope/sub-territory/entrepot failure modes do not apply: this is a national crop-area panel at exactly national scale, with per-km2 levels (e.g. ~2.0M ha wheat on 194k km2) plausible for interwar Romanian agriculture. What blocks verified_equal is the tail of the span. The Transylvania-sensitive crops step back up from 1944, not 1947: potatoes 142-202k ha in 1940-43 -> 247/234/255k in 1944/45/46 (postwar 1950-51: 229/243k); oats 433-527k -> 640/627/640k (postwar 520/467k); hemp 33-66k -> 85/87/84k. That matches the de facto Romanian/Soviet reoccupation of Northern Transylvania from August 1944 and its restoration to Romanian administration in March 1945, so the reporting territory almost certainly grows by ~43,000 km2 (+22%) partway through the observed 1940-1946 span. A territory that changes mid-span cannot equal any single polity, hence best_available. I stopped short of split_reroute because the 1944 signal is crop-specific and confounded with wartime/weather recovery (maize sits at 3.0-3.5M ha throughout 1940-46, showing no comparable step), and because the DB offers no 1944/45-1947 polity to split into - ROU-1947-2025 begins in 1947. ROU-1940-1947 remains the best available home for all seven years. The wiki page (reviewed, 8.8KB, 7 citations) is accurate and its documented Aug-1944 reoccupation independently corroborates the step I found in the numbers; it is neither suspect nor inadequate.
review.wiki_note: Data-side finding the page lacks: in the juan crop panel the Romania label's reporting territory is NOT constant across 1940-1946. The 1939->1940 break confirms the full triple cession (wheat -49% to 2,078k ha, barley -46%, potatoes -54%), but Transylvania-sensitive crops step back up from the 1944 harvest onward - potatoes 142-202k ha (1940-43) -> 247/234/255k (1944/45/46), oats 433-527k -> 640/627/640k, hemp 33-66k -> 85/87/84k, all at or above the 1950-51 postwar levels - consistent with the de facto reoccupation of Northern Transylvania from August 1944 and Romanian administration from March 1945. So roughly the last three years of this row's data are likely reported on ~237,000 km2 rather than the 194,000 km2 this page defines, and any per-area normalisation using this polygon will overstate intensity for 1944-1946.

verdict.basis: Inspected consolidated_layer_b.parquet directly: the fao1952 source carries 'France' as a distinct country label from 'Algeria', 'French North Africa Algeria', 'Saar', and 'France Saar' (a separate France-Saar customs-union entity, 1948-56) -- so the plain 'France' label under which these 324 rows are filed is metropolitan France only, not Algeria (administratively part of France at the time) and not the Saar protectorate, ruling out both the classic sub-territory fold-in and the union/empire-scope failure modes. Years observed for 'France' rows are 1937, 1947, 1948, 1949, 1950, 1951 (no continuous 1940-44 occupation-year data), so the WWII occupation/Vichy period -- which the wiki correctly notes did not change France's de jure metropolitan territory under the WHEP rule -- is not even represented in this assertion's span; the observed pre-war (1937) and post-war (1947-51) years both reflect the same restored metropolitan borders. Per-item meat-production magnitudes (beef/veal/mutton/pork each ~700-1900 thousand tonnes, aggregate a few million tonnes) show no discontinuity across 1937 vs 1947-51 that would indicate a territorial change, consistent with the already-verified population-series finding (France total population 41,200k in 1937, matching the 1936 census). The candidate's wiki page (draft status, but with 9 source citations for its polygon/territorial claims) independently documents metropolitan France as stable since 1919 except for a negligible 268 sq-mile Italy transfer post-WWII, which does not affect the FAO reporting territory. Together this establishes the source's reporting territory equals the candidate's territory and it stayed constant across the whole observed 1937-1951 span.
verdict.wiki_note: FAO 1952 (fao1952) reports 'France' as metropolitan France only: the source carries Algeria and the Saar as separate country labels ('Algeria', 'French North Africa Algeria', 'Saar', 'France Saar'), so this label does not fold in Algeria (then administratively part of France) or the Saar protectorate/customs-union territory. Confirms this label maps cleanly to FRA-1919-2025 with no sub-territory or union-scope contamination.

source_convention.convention: In fao1952, the plain country label 'France' denotes metropolitan France only. Algeria and the Saar (including the 1948-56 France-Saar customs union) are reported under separate distinct labels ('Algeria', 'French North Africa Algeria', 'Saar', 'France Saar'), not folded into 'France'.
source_convention.evidence: consolidated_layer_b.parquet fao1952 rows: distinct country values include 'France', 'Algeria', 'French North Africa Algeria', 'Saar', 'France Saar', 'France  Saar' as separate entities alongside plain 'France'.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes IIA's "france" label (1919-1945, 322 rows, 23 distinct years) to FRA-1919-2025 (metropolitan France, Treaty of Versailles to database ceiling). The wiki page is draft status (5195 bytes, 9 citations, no TODOs) and asserts metropolitan borders were stable 1919-2025 except a minor 1945 Italy transfer, treating the 1940-1944 Vichy/occupation period as a sovereignty gap only, not a territorial one. I independently inspected the raw layer_b data (consolidated_layer_b.csv): IIA years present for "france" are 1919-1925 and 1930-1945 (the 4-year gap 1926-1929 accounts for 23/27 years, unrelated to the war), and the label is used continuously through the occupation years with no separate Vichy/occupied-zone label in the data. Production magnitudes (wine, sugar) show normal wartime decline (e.g. wine tonnes ~6.7M in 1939 down to ~4.8M in 1940, recovering to ~4.3M in 1943-44) without an implausible step consistent with a large scope change, though a wine-area (ha) figure of 422,000 for 1943 vs 1,434,000/1,403,000 in neighboring years looks like a probable OCR/transcription defect in that one cell rather than a territorial signal. I also checked the France+Algeria fold-in concern flagged in the general instructions: data/final/source_label_lexicon.csv maps "algerie" to a separate "Algeria" label, so IIA reports Algeria distinctly from France — no colonial fold-in here. Web research turned up secondary evidence (FRED/NBER documentation of French agricultural series) that some French wartime agricultural statistics excluded Alsace-Lorraine during the German annexation of 1940-1944 — a real, if modest (Alsace is a small share of national wine/ag output), scope-narrowing risk during the occupation years that the wiki page does not address. Combined with the general point that occupation/annexation events occurring mid-span make a 1919-1945 span not provably constant-territory throughout, I judge this a best_available confirm rather than verified_equal: FRA-1919-2025 is clearly the right polity (no separate Vichy/occupied-France polity exists and none should be created for what looks like a partial, likely small-magnitude wartime reporting quirk rather than a full territorial split), but the territory cannot be certified as literally unchanged for the whole 1919-1945 span given the German annexation of Alsace-Lorraine during 1940-1944.
verdict.wiki_note: The page treats 1940-1944 purely as a sovereignty gap (Vichy/occupation) with no territorial effect, but doesn't address that Germany administratively annexed Alsace-Lorraine outright during 1940-1944 (separate from Vichy proper). Secondary sources (FRED/NBER documentation of French agricultural series, e.g. potato acreage) indicate some French wartime agricultural statistics excluded Alsace during this period. Raw IIA layer_b data (checked directly) shows "france" reported continuously through 1940-1945 with no separate Alsace/occupied-zone label, and no dramatic magnitude break correlated with occupation onset, so any exclusion is likely small (Alsace is a minor share of national wine/ag output) rather than a major scope error — but it means the reporting territory cannot be certified constant across the whole 1919-1945 span, so this should route as best_available rather than verified_equal.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes "Venezuela" (Mitchell trade/production data, 1873-1960, iso=ven) to VEN-1821-2025, the single continuous national Venezuela polity (1821-2025). Venezuela's national territory has been essentially stable since separation from Gran Colombia (1830): the Colombia land boundary was progressively demarcated (1932 agreement, later 1941 treaty) but this settled a previously disputed line rather than transferring controlled territory; the 1899 Paris arbitral award on the Guiana/Essequibo dispute concerned territory Venezuela never actually administered (it was under British control), so it did not change Venezuela's own reporting territory either. Staple magnitudes (cacao ~17k t, sugar ~20k t, beer ~50k t, fish ~69k t, meat ~81k t) are all plausible national-scale figures for Venezuela's population and tropical-agriculture profile across this period, with no entrepot or sub-territory scale mismatch. The label "venezuela" is a national-level identifier, not a province/colony fragment, so no fold-up risk. Given the 87-year span includes two boundary-demarcation episodes (1899 Guiana arbitration, 1932/1941 Colombia demarcation), I am treating the territory as best_available rather than asserting it was perfectly invariant to the km², even though no actual cession of Venezuelan-controlled land occurred.

The assertion routes IIA's "tunisia" label (1909-1945, n=313 rows) to TUN-1881-2025. This span sits entirely inside the French protectorate era (1881-1956); the WWII Axis occupation (1942-43) was military, not a border change. The candidate's wiki page (draft status, so treated as hypothesis) cites CShapes 2.0 recording three Tunisia entries (1886-1955, two 1956 entries) all with identical area (~15.19 sq deg / ~164,000 km2) -- an external geospatial-dataset fact, not just narrative assertion, indicating no territorial change across the whole 1886-2019 span, which covers the observed 1909-1945 window. The staple magnitudes (tobacco ~330t, grapes ~16,257 ha, wine ~40,000 ha, linseed, flax) are all plausible Mediterranean smallholder-agriculture outputs consistent with metropolitan Tunisia's climate and scale -- no entrepot/re-export signature, no sub-territory fold-up signature (label names the whole protectorate, not a province or district). No combined-reporting risk (Tunisia was a single French protectorate, not part of a union label during this period the way e.g. French Algeria was administratively France). Territory was constant throughout the observed span, so verified_equal is appropriate rather than best_available.

review.basis: Label "tunisia" in the IIA Annuaire international de statistique agricole, 1909-1945, denotes the French Protectorate of Tunisia, which the IIA reported as its own unit alongside (not inside) France, Algeria and Morocco. Scope check by magnitude is decisive: the vine series median ~40,000 ha (grape area 16,257 ha in a separate series) sits squarely on the documented Tunisian vineyard trajectory — steady growth from 1896, sharp acceleration 1926-1932, ~56,000 ha at the 1933 peak, then the 1934/1935 decrees forcing a 15% uprooting. That is one to two orders of magnitude below France proper (~1.5M ha) and roughly a tenth of Algeria (~400k ha), so the label is neither a metropole-inclusive aggregate nor an Algeria-inclusive North African total; tobacco ~330 t, linseed ~1,100 t and flax ~200 ha are likewise protectorate-scale, not empire-scale. Fold-up in the narrow direction is also excluded: the items are national crop aggregates, not a caidat/controle civil or a single estate district, and no sub-Tunisian granular polity exists or is implied. No entrepot problem — all items are grown in Tunisia's own Mediterranean north. Territorially the protectorate is essentially stable across 1909-1945 (independence 1956 lies outside the span; CShapes carries one unchanged polygon through 1955), so the routing to TUN-1881-2025 is correct. I withhold verified_equal only because the Franco-Ottoman convention of 19 May 1910 delimiting the Tunisia-Tripolitania boundary falls inside the observed span, and the candidate polygon is a 1886-vintage CShapes feature back- and forward-projected across the whole period; the difference is small in area terms but it is a within-span boundary fixation, so best_available is the honest label. The wiki page is a draft but not thin (3.1 kB, 5 citations, Biger 1995 plus CShapes) and its area figure ~164,000 km2 matches Tunisia's actual ~163,600 km2; I did not rely on it for the scope conclusion, which rests on the data magnitudes and external viticulture statistics.

source_convention.convention: The IIA yearbooks treat France's North African possessions as separate reporting units: Tunisia (and Algeria, Morocco) appear as their own country lines rather than being folded into France's totals, so an IIA 'France' series should not be assumed to include them and an IIA 'Tunisia' series is protectorate-only.
source_convention.evidence: Vine area under the Tunisia label (median ~40,000 ha, peaking near the documented ~56,000 ha Tunisian vineyard of 1933) is protectorate-scale, ~1/10 of Algeria and ~1/40 of metropolitan France, so the label cannot be an aggregate; all other staples (tobacco ~330 t, linseed ~1,100 t) are consistent.

verdict.basis: The label "china, mainland" is Mitchell's International Historical Statistics convention for distinguishing PRC-controlled mainland China from ROC/Taiwan — exactly matching candidate CHN-1950-2025 ("China (PRC)"), which per its wiki page's corrected polygon (9,369,260 km², post-Tibet-incorporation CShapes step) already includes Tibet from the row's 1950 start, cited independently against biger-1995's stated area (9,556,144 km², within 2.4%). The observed span 1950-1960 falls entirely within the row's start (territorial consolidation already complete by 1950) and well before the next territorial changes (1962 Aksai Chin, 1997 Hong Kong, 1999 Macau), so the reporting territory is constant across the whole observed span. Staple magnitudes (33.3M ha rice paddy, 23.3M ha wheat median) are of the right order of magnitude for full mainland Chinese agriculture, not a sub-territory, and not inflated by Taiwan (routed separately). No fold-up, entrepot, or combined-reporting concerns apply.

Assertion routes Mitchell's Iran production series (1905-1960, wheat/barley/rice/cotton/tobacco/cattle/horses) by ISO to IRN-1828-2025. The candidate wiki page (draft status but citing biger-1995's International Boundaries volume with page numbers, 10 source citations) documents that Persia/Iran's borders have been stable since the 1828 Treaty of Turkmenchay, with the only pre-1905 changes noted (1857 Anglo-Persian treaty on Afghan border) predating the observed span, and no territorial changes during 1905-1960 (the 1935 Persia->Iran rename and the 1941 Anglo-Soviet occupation were regime/sovereignty events, not border changes — Iran remained nominally sovereign over the same territory throughout the WWII occupation). This is consistent with well-established 20th-century history: Iran's 1905-1960 borders were essentially the same as today's, no annexations/cessions in that window (the 1907 Anglo-Russian Convention created spheres of influence, not territorial transfer). Staple magnitudes (wheat ~2.04M t, barley ~800k t, rice ~371k t, cotton lint ~20k t, tobacco ~13k t) are plausible in scale for Iran's population/agriculture in this period and show no discontinuity suggesting a scope change. The observed span (1905-1960) is a sub-range of the candidate's full 1828-2025 span, and within that sub-range the reporting territory equals the candidate's and stayed constant, so verified_equal is appropriate for THIS assertion even though the candidate's full row spans much more history.

The assertion covers Mitchell livestock/maize series labeled "Natal" for 1852-1894, entirely within the reviewed NAT-1843-1895 candidate's 1843-1895 span. The candidate's wiki page (reviewed, 2 source citations, no TODOs) documents that the colony's territory (core Natal south of the Tugela, ~43,663 km², CShapes feature 562) was constant until the 1895-04-23 Zululand incorporation — a change that falls just after the assertion's last observed year (1894), so no mid-span territorial shift is implicated. The neighbor_segments show a distinct successor polity (NAT-1895-1910, ~72,516 km²) taking over exactly at that boundary, consistent with "Natal" continuing to denote the same reporting unit throughout 1852-1894. Magnitudes (452k cattle, 345k sheep, 217k goats, 22k horses, ~1,212t maize) are plausible for a mid-sized 19th-century pastoral/settler colony and show no internal discontinuity suggesting a scope change. No sub-territory fold-up or entrepot risk applies (Natal was itself the producing unit, not a transit hub for this livestock/maize data). The page is adequately sourced for this specific claim, so confirm with verified_equal is warranted.

Assertion routes FAO 1952 "Australia" (1937-1951, meat/rye/hops/phosphoric-acid data) to AUS-1901-2025. The candidate's wiki page (reviewed, 4 source citations, no TODOs) documents the Commonwealth of Australia as federated 1901 from six colonies with stable borders since federation through the present (~7.69M km²) -- no territorial change occurs anywhere near the 1937-1951 observed span. The staple magnitudes in the bundle (meat ~286k tonnes, other meat ~47k tonnes, rye ~11k ha, hops ~1k ha, commercial phosphoric acid ~338k tonnes) are all plausible at national-Australia scale, not a fraction-of-territory or entrepot signature, and there is no sub-national or union-scope ambiguity comparable to the Sweden-Norway or Cisleithania cases (Australia federated as a single Commonwealth, not a personal union, and PNG/external territories are administered separately from the FAO's Australia agricultural statistics). The source_conventions note about FAO 1952 population-indicator mixing is not relevant here since the assertion's items are agricultural/production series, not population. No magnitude discontinuity or plausibility red flag across the 1937-1951 window. Territory is both equal to the candidate and constant across the whole span, so verified_equal applies.

review.basis: Reconstructing the territory first: the Commonwealth of Australia (six states + Northern Territory + ACT) was territorially unchanged across the entire observed span 1937-1951 — no annexation, cession, separation or occupation touched it; the only Australian-administered territorial events of the period (the 1949 merger of the Territory of Papua and the Territory of New Guinea into the Territory of Papua and New Guinea; Japanese wartime occupation of parts of New Guinea; Nauru's trusteeship) all concern EXTERNAL territories that were never part of the Commonwealth proper and that this database keeps as separate polities (TPAP-1906-1949, TNGU-1920-1949, PNG-1949-1975, NRU-1888-2025, NFK-1914-2025). Decisive scope evidence came from the source itself rather than from the wiki: the fao1952 assertion set carries separate labels "Papua", "New Guinea" (split 1937-1949 / 1950-1951, exactly tracking the 1949 amalgamation), "Netherlands New Guinea", "Nauru" and "Fiji", so the FAO 1952 yearbook demonstrably reports Australia's external territories as their own reporting units — the "Australia" label is neither an empire/union roll-up nor a combined-reporting label, and there is no sub-territory fold-up risk (no state- or district-level label is being pushed up to the Commonwealth). Magnitudes are consistent with Australia proper and with no scope shift: rye ~11k ha and hops ~1k ha are correct orders for minor Australian crops (hops confined to Tasmania/Victoria), meat ~286 kt is a component carcass-weight series within a total-meat output of roughly 1 Mt, and commercial phosphoric acid ~338 kt P2O5 matches Australia's exceptionally heavy superphosphate consumption (~1.5-2 Mt of superphosphate at ~20% P2O5) in the late 1940s — a magnitude that would be implausible for any smaller reporting scope. The candidate row AUS-1901-2025 spans the whole observed period with constant territory, so the reporting territory equals the candidate's for every year observed. The wiki page (reviewed, 2.1 KB, 4 Biger citations) states the same stable-borders position and is not the load-bearing evidence here; it is accurate as far as it goes, and its Biger note on the 1906 Papua transfer is not a contradiction since Papua is carried as its own polity and its own FAO label.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell rows labeled "mali" (iso=mli), years 1920-1959, to MLI-1890-1960 (French Sudan/Mali colonial territory, area 1,736,746 km² at the 1905 CShapes vintage). The candidate's own wiki page — a draft, but unusually well-documented with 3 source citations and an explicit, already-flagged territorial-vintage problem — shows that French Sudan/Mali's actual borders shifted repeatedly within the observed span itself: Upper Volta was carved out in 1919, dissolved back into Sudan in 1932, then reconstituted in 1947, with CShapes area figures ranging from ~1.25M to ~1.74M km² across seven time-steps entirely inside 1920-1959. This is the same continuous political/administrative entity (French Sudan → Mali) throughout, so the label is not combined-reporting nor a sub-territory fold-up nor an entrepot case — Mitchell's "Mali" series is plausibly this colony's own reported livestock/agriculture statistics (cattle median 1.34M, camels 51k, asses 154k are consistent orders of magnitude for a Sahelian territory this size). But because the reporting territory changed mid-span (Upper Volta out/in/out again), it cannot be verified_equal — the instruction's own rule (spans >30yr with boundary events => best_available) applies directly, and the page itself already documents and quantifies this (including a cross-check showing the 1905 polygon vintage double-counts ~272k km² against BFA-1947-1960). No existing more-granular polity exists to split into (Upper Volta-in-Sudan periods aren't separately coded), and the neighbor_segments entry (1960→MLI-1960-2025) confirms a clean handoff at independence. Confirm is therefore the right verdict, at best_available confidence, with no new wiki_note needed since the page already states the territorial-variability finding in more detail than I could add.

The wiki page (draft status but substantive: 2 source citations, no TODOs) already documents exactly the scope issue this assertion raises: French agricultural statistics for "Algeria" (IIA yearbooks, and by the same logic Mitchell, which compiles from the same official French colonial series) are collected on the three CIVIL departments (Alger, Oran, Constantine, ~575,511 km2 per IIA), not on the full colony polygon (2,442,683 km2 in ESRI:54034) that includes the Southern Territories/Sahara annexed 24 Dec 1902. The assertion's magnitudes (wheat ~1.30M ha, barley ~1.15M ha, oats ~174k ha, potatoes ~18k ha) are all cropland figures consistent with intensively-farmed northern Algeria and agronomically impossible for the Sahara, which produces essentially none of this - so the data is de facto reporting on the civil-departments sub-unit, exactly the gap the page already flags under issue 166 (basis_flag=review in data/final/source_stated_area_basis.csv). The page's own open question (oq-dza-civil-departments-as-a-reporting-unit) explicitly considered and declined to create a separate DZA-north polity for this sub-unit, since no polygon source exists for it and no data had yet arrived labelled that way - Mitchell's 'algeria' label is exactly that data, but it doesn't change the modelling decision already made. With no granular civil-departments polity in the DB, DZA-1902-1919 is the best available match, following the instruction to confirm a sub-territory label against its parent ONLY when the parent is the de facto reporting unit for that source - which is the case here (French colonial statistics rolled the civil departments up as 'Algeria', not as a separately-published entity). The territory (full colony incl. Sahara) is constant across the whole 1902-1918 observed span (Sahara annexed at candidate's 1902 start, no mid-span change), but since the reporting basis (civil departments) is narrower than the candidate's true territory (full colony), this is best_available rather than verified_equal.

source_convention.convention: Mitchell's colonial-Algeria agricultural series (crop areas in ha, production in tonnes) follow the same civil-departments reporting basis already documented for IIA under issue 166: they cover northern Algeria (the departments of Alger, Oran, Constantine, ~575,511 km2) rather than the full colony polygon including the Sahara Southern Territories annexed in 1902 (~2.44M km2). Tell: cropland magnitudes (wheat ~1.3M ha, barley ~1.15M ha) are agronomically plausible only for the northern departments, never the Sahara.
source_convention.evidence: Assertion algeria|mitchell|1902-1918 staple_magnitudes (wheat/barley/oats/potatoes areas) are consistent with northern Algeria's cultivated area and implausible if spread over the full colony including desert; matches the civil-departments-vs-colony gap already quantified for IIA in wiki/polities/dza-1902-1919.md and data/final/source_stated_area_basis.csv (issue 166).

verdict.wiki_note: Mitchell's 'algeria' agricultural series (crop areas/production, 1902-1918) shows the same civil-departments-vs-full-colony reporting gap already documented here for IIA (issue 166): the data's cropland magnitudes are plausible only for northern Algeria (Alger/Oran/Constantine), not the Sahara included in this polity's polygon. This corroborates that the gap is a property of French colonial agricultural statistics generally, not specific to the IIA yearbooks, but does not resolve oq-dza-civil-departments-as-a-reporting-unit since no separate polygon/polity exists to route it to.

verdict.basis: Assertion routes Mitchell's "China, Taiwan Province of" label (1945-1960, ISO twn) to TWN-1945-2025. The candidate's wiki page (draft status, but backed by 3 source citations from Biger 1995) documents Taiwan island + Pescadores, area ~36,000 km², territorially stable since the 1945 retrocession with no border change through the observed span. Mitchell/UN statistical convention names Taiwan "China, Taiwan Province of" precisely to denote the ROC-administered island as distinct from mainland China — this is a naming convention, not evidence of combined mainland+island reporting. Staple magnitudes (rice paddy ~786,000 ha, sugar cane ~122,000 t, sweet potatoes ~238,000 ha) are consistent with known mid-20th-century Taiwan island agricultural scale (far too small for mainland China, plausible for a 36,000 km² island), so there is no entrepot/combined-reporting red flag. The observed span (1945-1960) is fully inside the candidate's territorial-stability period (1945 retrocession to present), with no annexation/cession/occupation event splitting it. Verdict: confirm, verified_equal.

The observed span 1919-1939 falls entirely inside BGR-1919-1940's stable interwar borders: Bulgaria's territory was fixed by the Treaty of Neuilly (27 Nov 1919) and did not change again until the Treaty of Craiova returned Southern Dobruja on 7 September 1940 -- after the last observed year (1939). This is well-documented interwar history independent of the draft wiki page (which is largely self-citing to the CSV but whose factual claims about Neuilly/Craiova dates and the ~103,000 km2 stable extent match the historical record). The staple magnitudes (wine ~89k t, cotton seed/lint in the low thousands of ha, hemp yarn ~3,300 t) are all plausible for a mid-sized Balkan agrarian state and show no discontinuity suggesting a scope change. Neighbor segments correctly bookend to BGR-1918-1919 (pre-Neuilly) and BGR-1940-2025 (post-Craiova/WWII), consistent with the territorial-change rule. No union/empire-scope issue (Bulgaria was never part of a larger union), no sub-territory fold-up (this is the full national polity, not a component), and no entrepot/re-export concern for these commodities.

review.basis: I pulled the raw IIA/Bulgaria rows (450) out of ~/Nextcloud/whep/layer_b/consolidated_layer_b.csv and read the series 1909-1945 before consulting any prose. Arithmetic first: the levels are those of a ~100,000 km2, ~6M-person Balkan agrarian state, not of a union or an empire -- vineyards 48k ha (1922) rising to ~89k ha (1934-38) yielding 75k-230k t wine (weather-driven, ~1-2M hl, exactly interwar Bulgaria's documented range); silk cocoons ~1.1-2.3k t; hemp fibre 1-4k t; cotton 787 ha in 1909 climbing to 55,000 ha by 1938 with seed output 15-22k t. That cotton trajectory is the fingerprint of the Bulgarian state's 1930s cotton-promotion policy in the Plovdiv/Chirpan/Haskovo south, and it is far too small to be anyone's aggregate of a larger unit. No fold-up risk in the other direction either: "bulgaria" names the whole state, Bulgaria had no colonies or union partner, and there is no entrepot story (these are field crops on Bulgarian soil). Combined reporting is excluded -- there is no second Bulgarian polity to fold in. Continuity across our period splits is clean: nothing at the 1919 or the 1939/40 boundary looks like a territorial step. Every apparent jump is vintage or policy (wine 1919 75.8k t / 1920 38.4k / 1921 127.6k is weather; sugar 1918 64.4k t is the war-time spike). The one genuine scope signal actually supports the split rather than contradicting it: cotton area halves 1918 2,944 ha -> 1919 1,534 ha, consistent with Bulgaria shedding its war-time occupied Aegean/Thracian south, i.e. the 1919 row already reports on reduced borders. IIA's own footnote file (pipelines/polity-autoimprove/state/iia_territorial_notes.csv) carries no territorial caveat for Bulgaria at all. The draft wiki page's territorial claim (post-Neuilly, ~103,000 km2, stable through the interwar, ending at Craiova 1940) matches what I independently know of Neuilly and Craiova and matches the arithmetic, so I did not need to lean on it. Why best_available rather than verified_equal: the observed span opens in 1919, and the Treaty of Neuilly was only signed 27 Nov 1919 and entered into force 9 Aug 1920, so Western Thrace (~8,600 km2) and the Western Outlands (~1,545 km2) were still de jure Bulgarian for part of the 1919 reporting year while the candidate's CShapes-1919 polygon is already the post-Neuilly shape. The territory therefore did not stay strictly constant across the whole 1919-1939 span, even though it was constant for 1920-1939 and the deviation is under ~10% of area in a single year of eighteen. Craiova (+7,700 km2, Sept 1940) falls outside the observed span, so it does not contaminate this routing.
review.wiki_note: Boundary vintage at the row's own start: Neuilly was signed 27 Nov 1919 but only entered into force 9 Aug 1920, so IIA's 1919 figures may sit on pre-Neuilly borders (Western Thrace ~8,600 km2, Western Outlands ~1,545 km2) rather than on the CShapes-1919 polygon this row uses; the page currently asserts stability "throughout the interwar period" without noting this. The IIA series itself suggests the effect is small -- cotton area halves from 2,944 ha (1918) to 1,534 ha (1919), i.e. the reporting had already dropped the war-time occupied south. Separately, a data-quality flag on the source rather than the polity: the IIA Bulgaria rows include "other berries and fruits of the genus vaccinium n.e.c." at ~4,000-5,000 ha and up to 68,100 t, which is agronomically impossible for Bulgarian blueberry/cranberry cultivation and is almost certainly a mis-mapped item code (a Bulgarian fruit or rose-petal series folded into an n.e.c. bucket).

verdict.basis: Mitchell reports "Mozambique" 1901-1960 (285 rows across 58 years) for staple agricultural/livestock commodities (sugar cane, groundnuts, cattle, goats, swine). The candidate MOZ-1891-1975 is Portuguese Mozambique, a single colonial territory whose borders were fixed by the 1891 Anglo-Portuguese treaty agreements and remained unchanged until independence in 1975 (per the wiki page, sourced to Biger 1995 and CShapes 2.0, which shows no area change between 1891 and the 1975 successor transition). The observed span 1901-1960 falls entirely within this stable-border period, well before any territorial change. "Mozambique" here is the whole colony/national reporting unit, not a sub-territory (no concessionary-company or provincial fragmentation of the data label), and the magnitudes (hundreds of thousands of cattle/goats, tens of thousands of tonnes of sugar/groundnuts) are plausible for a colony this size, not requiring an entrepot or double-count explanation. The wiki page is thin (draft status, 1 source citation) but its core territorial claim (fixed Portuguese colonial borders 1891-1975) is externally corroborated by the cited Biger 1995 concessionary-companies passage and is uncontradicted, so it is adequate to support (not the sole basis for) this specific claim.

Assertion routes FAO 1952 "Japan" (1947-1951, agricultural production items: meat, milk, poultry, groundnuts) to JPN-1945-1952 ("Japan (occupied)", 1945-1952, area 377,657 km2, home islands only, all colonies/Ryukyus stripped). Wiki page is draft status but carries 5 source citations to biger-1995, which I independently verified in wiki/sources/biger-1995.md: p.329 states Japan's total land area as 145,870 sq mi (377,657 sq km), home islands, no land boundaries -- matching the polygon area exactly. The page explicitly documents that Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa, ~2,271 km2) are administered separately (US military government, not SCAP) and that FAO-1952 "Ryukyu Islands" rows route to a different polity (RYU-1945-1972), confirming the source itself distinguishes the two labels rather than lumping them -- so no sub-territory fold-up or entrepot risk for the "Japan" label itself. Neighbor segment (1936-1937 -> JPN-1895-1945, pre-war Greater Japan with colonies) is consistent with the predecessor/successor chain and the 1945 territorial break (surrender, loss of Taiwan/Korea/Sakhalin/Pacific mandates). Staple magnitudes (meat ~69k t, milk ~122k t, poultry ~252k heads) are plausible in scale for postwar depleted home-islands agriculture and show no discontinuity flag. The observed span (1947-1951) lies entirely within the occupied period (1945-1952) with no territorial change during that window, so verified_equal is appropriate.

The assertion routes Juan's "germany" label (280 rows, 1938-1944) to DEU-1938-1945 by ISO match. The candidate's wiki page (draft status, but substantial: 9008 bytes, 13 source citations, no TODO markers) documents that this polity's territory was NOT constant across the row: 1938-1939 the CShapes 1938 polygon (~541,000 km2, Germany+Austria+Sudetenland) fits well; 1939-1942 Germany incorporated ~138,000 km2 more (Bohemia-Moravia protectorate, Danzig-West Prussia, Wartheland, Alsace-Lorraine, Luxembourg) that the polygon does not capture, an under-coverage the page itself flags and links to elevated wheat/sugar magnitudes from Czech and Polish agricultural regions; 1943-1945 the territory contracted again as occupation reversed, making the polygon an over-statement. This territorial narrative matches standard WWII history (Anschluss 1938, Munich 1938, Bohemia-Moravia protectorate March 1939, invasion of Poland September 1939 with incorporation of western Polish Reichsgaue, administrative absorption of Alsace-Lorraine/Luxembourg 1940-41, then front collapse from late 1942) independently of the page's own assertion, so I treat the territorial-change claim as corroborated rather than circular, even though the page's overall wiki_status is draft. No finer-grained existing polity covers the 1939-1942 peak-expansion configuration (the page explicitly documents that a 3-way split was proposed and deferred for lack of a usable polygon), so there is no better routing target available within the current DB -- confirm is correct, but because the reporting territory changed substantially mid-span (expansion then contraction) rather than staying constant, this cannot be verified_equal; it is best_available. No contradiction found in the page; it is unusually thorough for a draft, so no page_suspect or page_inadequate finding, and I have nothing new to add to wiki_note.

The candidate's wiki page, though flagged wiki_status draft, is substantively sourced (6 citations, direct CShapes 2.0 raw-file inspection across three time-steps) and shows the polity's area held constant at 4,894,456 km2 across the whole 1914-1936 observed span, with the only real territorial changes (a frontier adjustment and the Burma separation) falling right at the 1914 start and 1937 end boundaries, not inside the span. The magnitude ~4.89M km2 is consistent with British India including Burma (pre-1937), matching the IIA data's very large staple magnitudes (jute ~1.16M ha, cotton seed ~2.2M ha, tea ~262k tonnes) which are plausible only for the whole subcontinental+Burma territory reported as 'India' in that era's agricultural statistics, not a sub-region. Neighbor segments route cleanly to the adjacent predecessor/successor polities with no overlap, and the polities_database.csv row confirms dates/codes match.

review.basis: I pulled the 393 raw `iia`/`india` rows out of ~/Nextcloud/whep/layer_b/consolidated_layer_b.parquet and read the per-year series rather than the bundle's medians. Scope test (the decisive one): cotton area runs 8.5-11.3M ha (21-28M acres) through 1909-1933. British provinces alone carried only ~15M acres of cotton in the interwar years; the extra third sat in Hyderabad, Central India, Rajputana and Baroda, so this label is the whole Indian Empire (provinces + princely states), not the Vol-I "British India provinces" table -- i.e. the candidate's territory, not a sub-territory. Upward-scope test in the other direction: tea area 225-330k ha (0.55-0.81M acres) and tea output ~167kt (~368M lb) match India alone; had the label folded in Ceylon (another ~0.5M acres / ~230M lb) both would be roughly double, so this is not a British-Empire aggregate. Jute 1.0-1.4M ha and tobacco 0.40-0.55M ha are likewise all-India-scale, and none of the crops present is an entrepot/re-export tell (all are agronomically native to the territory). Vintage/continuity: every series is smooth straight across our 1913/1914 split (cotton 10.12->9.94M ha, jute 1.18->1.36, tea 246,962->252,786, tobacco 418,213->420,161), so the same reporting territory spans IND-1893-1914 and IND-1914-1937 -- the split is ours, not the source's, and no step indicates a scope change inside 1914-1936. India's borders were in fact constant over the span; the row's endpoints are the 1914 frontier settlement and the 1937 Burma separation, both real. No combined reporting (no second polity is folded in), and the French/Portuguese enclaves the candidate polygon now subtracts (4,246 km2, 0.09%) would not have been in a Government-of-India return either. Why best_available rather than verified_equal: I could not establish from the publication itself whether IIA's "India" totals included Burma (inside the candidate until 1937, ~14% of its area) -- for these particular crops Burma is negligible, so the magnitudes cannot decide it -- and the Agricultural Statistics of India's princely-state coverage expanded over the period, so the reporting *coverage* drifted even where the territory did not. Neither defect changes the routing; both forbid claiming exact equality. Web searching turned up the Vol I (British provinces) / Vol II (Indian States) structure of the underlying compilation but no digitised IIA territorial footnote for India, so the scope conclusion rests on the data's own magnitudes, not on the source's prose or on the draft wiki page.
review.wiki_note: Magnitude evidence on the label's scope, which the page does not have: IIA "india" reports the whole Indian Empire including the princely states, not the British provinces alone -- cotton area is 8.5-11.3M ha (21-28M acres) where the provinces alone held ~15M acres -- and it excludes Ceylon (tea 225-330k ha, ~167kt, i.e. India-only levels). All series run smoothly through the 1913/1914 boundary, so the reporting territory is continuous with IND-1893-1914. Two open items: whether Burma is inside these totals is undetermined (none of the crops present is Burma-weighted), and the layer-B iia values for this label carry scale corruption -- coffee 1924-25 recorded as 34 and 45 ha against ~80,000 ha neighbours, sesame and groundnut series flipping between ~1,000 and ~2.5M ha, cotton 1934-37 stored as 0 -- so per-row magnitudes here should not be used without a scale screen.

verdict.basis: The assertion covers Canada, FAO 1952 label, years 1949-1951, routed to CAN-1949-2025 (modern Canada, post-Newfoundland-accession, 1949-2025, stable external borders per CShapes 2.0 and biger-1995). The candidate's wiki page is status "reviewed" with 4 source citations and is not a thin stub. It already documents the exact relevant check: a Verification notes entry dated 2026-07-24 states FAO 1952 "Canada" 1948-1951 meat/poultry/pesticide series show no magnitude break across the 31 March 1949 Newfoundland accession, consistent with continuous national-scope reporting. The assertion's observed span (1949-1951) falls entirely after the accession date and entirely within the candidate's 1949-2025 span, so there is no union-vs-component ambiguity (Newfoundland is already absorbed for the whole observed span) and no boundary-vintage or combined-reporting concern. Staple magnitudes (meat ~426k tonnes, poultry ~1,524k heads) are plausible for a country of Canada's scale and show no discontinuity per the wiki's own verification note and the neighbor_segments entry (1931-1948 -> CAN-1886-1949, a distinct predecessor row), confirming territorial continuity rather than a split need. This is a straightforward, non-controversial match: no empire/union scope issue (Canada was never merged into a larger reporting union in this era), no sub-territory fold-up (Canada is the full national unit, not a component), and no entrepot/re-export concern for these commodities. Confirm as verified_equal since the reporting territory equals the candidate's and stayed constant (post-accession, stable borders) across the whole 1949-1951 observed span.

The assertion's observed span (1926-1960) sits entirely inside candidate UGA-1926-1962's period (27 Sep 1926 - 8 Oct 1962), which per the wiki/CShapes is the stable post-1926-boundary-adjustment British Protectorate of Uganda, unchanged through independence in Oct 1962 -- i.e. no territorial change occurs anywhere within the 1926-1960 observed window. The label 'uganda' in Mitchell is a plain national/ISO match (route=iso, iso_in_data=uga), not a sub-territory or union label, so none of the fold-up/union-scope failure modes apply. Staple magnitudes (coffee green median 19,150 t, cattle 2.5M head, goats 2.3M head) are plausible for Uganda's actual size (~240,000 km2) and its known role as a major colonial robusta-coffee and pastoral-cattle producer, and the immediately preceding neighbor_segments (UGA-1902-1910, UGA-1910-1926) show the same iso-based routing continuing smoothly with no scope discontinuity implied at the 1926 boundary. The wiki page (draft) documents the 1926 CShapes area reduction as occurring right at the start of this period (not mid-span) and the territory is described as constant through 1962, which is independently consistent with the data's full-span coverage.

The assertion routes IIA "viet nam" trade rows (1930-1944, 273 rows) to VNM-1887-1954, the Vietnam-only component of French Indochina (Cochinchina+Annam+Tonkin, ~326k km2), distinct from the full federation FID-1887-1954 (~699k km2). The wiki page (draft status but 2 source citations and substantial detail) explains this fold-up explicitly: IIA reports "viet nam" separately from "indochina", with rice-paddy area ratios (~2.1-2.4M ha vs ~5.5-6M ha) independently corroborating the ~47% area ratio consistent with 326k/699k km2. This is the correct direction of the sub-territory check -- VNM is itself an existing granular polity (not folded up into the larger parent FID), so routing here is proper rather than a fold-up error. The observed span 1930-1944 falls entirely within the stable 1893-1954 CShapes polygon window (post-Laos-transfer, pre-Geneva-Accords), so the reporting territory did not change during the assertion's span. Staple magnitudes (cotton lint ~598 ha, groundnuts/tobacco/coffee ~2000 ha medians) are plausible smallholder crop areas for Vietnam's agricultural land and show no entrepot/agronomic-impossibility red flags. The page's polygon-vintage discussion (documented under Decisions, including a corrected 2026-08-05 fix for a tie-break bug) shows independent verification work beyond a bare CSV-derived stub, so I do not consider it page_inadequate or page_suspect.

The assertion routes 273 rows of IIA "zimbabwe" data (1911-1945, 30 distinct years) to ZWE-1900-1953 (Southern Rhodesia under BSAC/colonial administration). The candidate's wiki page (status draft, but with 4 source citations and specific CShapes+Biger documentation) establishes that this polity's territory was stable for the entire 1900-1953 span: Northern Rhodesia was already separated by 1900, CShapes records no boundary change until the 1953 Federation, and the 1923 shift to self-governing colony status was a regime change without territorial change. The observed data span (1911-1945) falls entirely inside this stable 1900-1953 window, so there is no mid-span annexation/cession to worry about. The commodities (tobacco, cotton, groundnuts, dry beans) are agronomically consistent with Southern Rhodesia's actual colonial-era export agriculture (tobacco especially is the classic Rhodesian staple), with no entrepot/re-export red flags. The "zimbabwe" label plausibly denotes Southern Rhodesia specifically (not a combined Rhodesias union or the later Federation), matching known IIA/League of Nations statistical practice of reporting Southern Rhodesia separately from Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland pre-1953. No evidence of sub-territory fold-up or combined-reporting distortion.

review.basis: Territory first: the observed span 1911-1945 lies entirely inside a period in which Southern Rhodesia's borders did not change. Its limits were fixed by the 1898 Order in Council; the 1911 amalgamation of North-Western and North-Eastern Rhodesia created Northern Rhodesia north of the Zambezi and did not touch the southern territory; the 1923 end of BSAC rule and grant of responsible government was constitutional, not territorial; the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, which would have made the label ambiguous, only begins in 1953, well after the span. So one polity CAN equal the reporting territory for the whole span, and ZWE-1900-1953 is that polity. Scope and combined-reporting were checked in the source files rather than from the wiki: /home/usuario/whep-polities/pipelines/polity-autoimprove/state/iia_territorial_notes.csv shows the IIA yearbooks carry "british south rhodesia" as its own reporting unit (with owned-by-europeans/natives splits 1939-1945), and matched_rows.parquet carries a separate normalized country "zambia" (British North Rhodesia) with its own IIA rows -- so "zimbabwe" here is Southern Rhodesia alone, not a "Rhodesias" aggregate and not a union with Nyasaland. Sub-territory fold-up is not in play: the label is the whole colony, not a district or mining field. Magnitudes corroborate independently: IIA tobacco area runs 1,067 ha (1911) to ~3,000-3,900 ha (1919-1924) to 17,000 ha (1933-36) to 35,000 ha (~87,000 acres) in 1945, the well-known Southern Rhodesian flue-cured tobacco trajectory -- far too large for Northern Rhodesia, far too small for a Rhodesias+Nyasaland aggregate; the 1924 cotton spike (25,437 ha) matches the Southern Rhodesian cotton boom of 1924/25. No step change in any series that would signal a mid-span scope shift. Not an entrepot case (area/production series for crops the highveld actually grows). The wiki page is draft, but its territorial description (Southern Rhodesia, 390,610 km2, Zambezi/Mozambique/South Africa/Botswana bounds, no boundary change 1900-1953) agrees with the independent reconstruction; the verdict does not rest on it.
review.wiki_note: Data-quality issue in the IIA series routed here, not an error on the page: alongside the coherent tobacco AREA series (1,067 ha in 1911 to 35,000 ha in 1945) there are "tobacco, unmanufactured" TONNAGE rows of 460,200 t and 1,050,600 t (year missing) and 2,141,800 t for 1945 -- two to three orders of magnitude above plausible Southern Rhodesian output (~15,000 t in 1945), almost certainly an unconverted imperial-weight or parsing error rather than a territorial-scope problem. Also, IIA reports Southern Rhodesia split by "owned by europeans"/"owned by natives" for 1939-1945, so totals and ownership sub-series must not be summed.

verdict.basis: Mitchell's "Cuba" label reports on the island of Cuba, a single geographic unit with no land boundaries that has been constant at ~110,861 km2 across the entire 1850-1960 observed span, per Biger 1995 (cited in the wiki page with source citations, not merely an unreviewed guess about territory).
